title: Field lattice standup snapshot — Oct 11 2028
content:
Weekly snapshot from the field lattice standup (notes, quick results, and next steps)

Date: 2028-10-11
Attendees: Mariana, Ethan, Liu, Sara, Jules (partial)

One-line summary:
- Focus this week: surface and triage token-stutter regressions in 4-bit weight-only quant runs, finalize probe eval for summarization suite, and prep onboarding checklist for arlene-13b-v2. Rough wins: microbatch tuning recovered p95 latency by ~18% on small sequences; outstanding: intermittent KV-cache thrash at mid-sequence under certain prefix patterns.

Current context / motivation:
- We want predictable SLOs for compact quant models across hosted and dedicated. Several customers reported periodic latency spikes for 4-bit variants during long-turn dialogues. Onboarding new models requires we surface these edgecases early in the lab so rollouts don't hit production surprises.

Quick metrics snapshot (averaged across test harness)
- Test rig: 2xA40, 24 CPU threads, default kv-cache enabled, microbatch size varied
- Model: arlene-13b-v2 (baseline fp16) vs arlene-13b-v2-q4_wonly (4-bit weight-only)
- Throughput (tokens/sec): fp16 = 410, q4 = 1220 (peak, short sequences)
- p50 latency (single request, 64 tokens): fp16=46ms, q4=18ms
- p95 latency (single request, 512 tokens): fp16=380ms, q4=520ms (regression observed)
- Eval metrics (summarization suite, ROUGE-L): fp16=0.512, q4=0.504 (delta -0.008)
- Perplexity on open-web dev: fp16=12.3, q4=13.2 (delta +0.9)

Notes on anomaly: mid-sequence stutter
- Repro pattern: with certain prefix tokens that cause kv-cache eviction patterns (identified approx tokens containing long numeric sequences + repeated named entities), q4_wonly runs show a repeated latency spike starting around token 140-180, then recovery. Not present in fp16 runs.
- Hypothesis 1: quantized matmul path triggers an alternate kernel path for long kv-cache lookups causing cache-line contention on host->device transfers.
- Hypothesis 2: microbatch aggregation + continuous batching interacts with KV prefetch evictions; we flush and re-warm caches, creating a visible spike.
- Quick repro: script "repro/stutter-sim.sh" (linked in PR) reproduces ~70% of the cases locally.

Experiments run this week (short notes)
1) Microbatch sweep (Ethan)
   - microbatch sizes: [1,2,4,8]; continuous batching window: 10ms, 20ms
   - result: size=2 + 10ms window best tradeoff — p95 down ~18% for typical dialogues, throughput unchanged for short seqs.
2) KV prefetch disable test (Liu)
   - disabling prefetch removed spike in 90% repro cases but increased overall p50 by ~12ms.
   - suggests prefetch interference root cause.
3) Weight-only vs weight+activation quant probe (Sara)
   - activation quant (q4_act) shows slightly worse perplexity (+1.4) but eliminates stutter in many cases; memory growth forces 16GB minimum.
4) Sparse attention toggle (Jules)
   - enabling sparse attention on tail windows reduced KV pressure but accuracy dip on summarization tail scope substantial (-0.018 ROUGE-L).

Decisions / triage
- Short-term: ship a conservative rollout policy for q4_wonly with KV-prefetch=false by default for dedicated small-GPU SKUs. Add automatic fallback to fp16 when persistent stutter seen for 3+ requests in a session. (Action: Mariana to draft rollout config)
- Mid-term: invest in kernel path tracing for the q4 matmul to identify host transfer hotspots. (Action: Liu + infra)
- Long-term: revisit activation quant recipe and mixed q4_w+q8_act hybrid for 16GB-class configs to reduce memory while avoiding stutter. (Action: Sara to prototype)

Onboarding checklist for arlene-13b-v2 (current status)
- Baseline perf/accuracy tests: complete (fp16 baseline)
- Quant recipes run: w-only q4 (done), w+act q4 (prototype), q8 hybrid (not started)
- KV-cache compatibility tests: failing intermittent stutter for q4_wonly (in progress)
- Memory footprint matrix across SKUs: measured; 8GB insufficient for w+act, 16GB OK
- Security / license check: model license OK for hosted-catalog use; legal thumbs-up received 2028-09-29
- Deployable artifact produced: yes (container tag: arlene-13b-v2-20281010)

Eval notes
- Summarization suite scaled to 1200 prompts (diverse doc lengths). q4_wonly drop in ROUGE-L is small (-0.008) but we see qualitative failure modes in numeric fidelity. Recommend adding numeric fidelity probes to regression alerts.
- Human-in-the-loop sampling: ran small HITL run (n=48) on long-form summarization; users reported more hallucinations on dates/numbers for q4 runs. Need targeted evals.

Open questions / friction points
- Is the stutter reproducible across different driver versions? We have one datapoint on driver 525 and one on driver 542; pattern shows up on both but variance differs. Need matrix run.
- Does the runtime currently combine microbatching and kv-prefetch cancelation in an atomic safe way? Potential race causing double eviction.
- How much of the observed delta is dataset-specific (e.g., the summ-suite has high entity repetition)? Need to sanity-check on web-scrape dev set.

Action items (owners & rough due)
- Mariana: draft a canary rollout config with KV-prefetch off for compact SKUs, include automatic fallback logic (due 2028-10-14)
- Liu: kernel path trace + driver matrix runs (start 10/12, deliver diagnostics by 10/18)
- Ethan: add numeric-fidelity probes to summarization eval harness and re-run (due 10/16)
- Sara: prototype q4_w + q8_act hybrid and report mem/accuracy tradeoffs (POC by 10/20)
- Jules: run sparse-attention ablation across the full dev suite to quantify accuracy tax (results by 10/19)

Notes to self / to-dos that are informal:
- We should capture traces (nvtx + custom tags) around token 120-200 window and compare memory map before/after spike.
- Consider a light-weight agent to detect repeated entity prefixes and tag them for fallback to fp16 in real-time.
- Ping infra about scheduling a long driver/regression sweep; this will take ~3 days of queue time on the lab cluster.

Misc/brainstorm (scratchpad)
- Could we take advantage of prefix caching at the request router level (route small repeated prefixes to a warm partition) to avoid KV churn?
- If host<->device transfer is the culprit, maybe a pinned pinned-buffer pool for kv tokens could amortize allocation cost.
- Do we want a short-term heuristic: if p95 exceeds baseline by 2x for >5 requests, throttle and escalate to fallback? (tradeoff UX vs reliability)

Appendix (repro commands, quick links)
- repro script: scripts/repro/stutter-sim.sh (local)
- perf harness: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-probe (PR #213)
- quick logs: s3://redwood-lab/logs/arlene-q4/2028-10-11/*

End of snapshot.

-- Mariana
